entries.english:
Rent from properties on the hill of Wildenberg Castle. Heinrich Tentz owes for one holding 15 shillings of Heller at both Walpurgis and Michaelmas, 30 eggs at Easter, three cheeses at Pentecost and three at Christmas, and one chicken each in autumn and at Shrovetide. Konrad Schuchman owes for a fief 7½ shillings at each of the two terms, 20 eggs, two cheeses at each feast, and the same chickens. Otto Rosentrit owes the same as the preceding tenant. Fritz Rephun owes for a plot and garden two shillings at each term and one chicken at Shrovetide; Wolfhard Straubinger owes the same. Heinrich Frech owes for a plot and garden 30 Heller at each term and a Shrovetide chicken.

The preceding properties are, as Dietrich von Redwitz asserts, his and his heirs’ castle-guard tenure for as long as he or his heirs reside personally in the castle. Dietrich also holds three fiefs there on the same terms and cultivates them himself. Konrad von Rosenberch owes for a fief nine shillings at each term, 30 Easter eggs, two cheeses each at Pentecost and Christmas, and one chicken each in autumn and at Shrovetide.

The following are smallholders: Ulrich Halberfreunt owes 10½ shillings at each term and, as regards cheeses and chickens, the same as the preceding tenant. Otto Raubennach owes six shillings at each term, 20 eggs, one cheese at each feast, and one chicken each in autumn and at Shrovetide. Rudolf owes for a plot and garden three shillings at each term, 12 eggs, one cheese at each feast, and a Shrovetide chicken. Otto the cook owes for a plot and garden two shillings at each term and a Shrovetide chicken. Konrad the weaver owes for an almost deserted plot 12 Heller at each term and nothing else. Redlein owes two shillings at each term for a plot and nothing else; Hermann the hunter owes four shillings at each term for a plot and nothing else. Wolfhard Turnman owes two shillings at each term for a plot and garden. Petzolt Prager and Strazenhauser each occupy a plot outside the castle for which they pay nothing.

The bishop has a farm there, estimated at one and a half holdings of arable land, which Fritz Ruffus cultivates for half the produce. That half is valued at 11 pounds of Heller, including meadows yielding about four wagonloads of hay. A total is indicated for Heller, chickens, eggs and cheeses, excluding the farm. A marginal note concerns the cleared Aichlopp wood, the rent and tithe of its fields, and their becoming vacant at Michaelmas in the year 57; it says the property is claimed to belong to Weissmeun but was found to belong to Wildenberg, as shown below.

research: The episcopal rent register (Urbar B) was begun in 1348 and contains later additions. The marginal note refers to Michaelmas in the year 57, probably 1357; this is the date used for this entry, although the note does not establish when the main rent list was written. The register records episcopal properties and dues, and also includes legal and administrative material. Sources: https://germania-sacra-datenbank.uni-goettingen.de/files/books/AF%202%20von%20Guttenberg%20Bamberg.pdf; https://fis.uni-bamberg.de/server/api/core/bitstreams/a876cd8a-4b04-44e9-a118-2da70698b41e/content.
